title: The 59-Game Revolution: Don Nelson's Forgotten Impact on the Knicks
description:
Don Nelson, the second-winningest coach in NBA history, passed away on August 9, 2026, at age 86. While his legendary career spanned decades with the Bucks, Mavericks, and Warriors, his 59-game tenure with the Knicks in 1995-96 remains a fascinating footnote. Nelson's revolutionary pace-and-space philosophy clashed with New York's physical, defensive identity, leading to his mid-season firing despite a 34-25 record. His proposal to trade Patrick Ewing for a young Shaquille O'Neal revealed the tension between innovation and tradition.

This episode explores Nelson's brief but significant time with the Knicks, examining how his forward-thinking approach—rejected in 1995—became the blueprint for modern basketball. From developing Dirk Nowitzki to drafting Stephen Curry, Nelson's influence shaped the NBA we know today. The 2026 champion Knicks, ironically, now play a style that echoes what Nelson preached three decades ago. A deep dive into basketball philosophy, organizational identity, and the price of being ahead of your time.
